title: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

sense.text:
Pastor Pam, Philip Anthony Mitchell, stood up and said that Ephesians 2 was about joining blacks and whites together through Christ: that the dividing line was destroyed and all of us were made into one family, and that black people don’t like white people for something they cannot control. That is a lie. Did he forget about slavery? So go back and read who the letter is talking about.

“That at that time ye were without Christ, being aliens from the commonwealth of Israel, and strangers from the covenants of promise, having no hope, and without God in the world.” There is a lot in that sentence. The strangers are Israelites, scattered as strangers. And Christians never address the covenants of promise. The only time the Lord made a covenant with all nations was in Genesis 9, when he said he would not destroy the world by water again. Every other covenant he made with Abraham and his seed, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and with no other nation.

Even ChatGPT, asked whether God ever entered into a covenant with all nations or only Israel, had to answer that the covenant of the law at Sinai was only with Israel, not with all nations, and that the new covenant as prophesied is with the house of Israel and the house of Judah. They know it, but they still try to force this all-nations-can-be-saved doctrine. It is not in the Bible. The covenant of promise is only with Israel.

“But now in Christ Jesus ye who sometimes were far off are made nigh by the blood of Christ.” The ones far off are Israel, scattered abroad, and Christ brought them near. We deal with precepts: Christians like to run to the Greek and to other books, but we stick to the scriptures and stay within our book.

“For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us.” Two words have to be dealt with: our, and us. Our peace, not everybody’s peace. Reading from verse 12 down to 14, the us is the nation of Israel; these Ephesians in Ephesus are Israelites scattered in Ephesus. This is not talking about blacks and whites coming together.

The both made one are the two houses, the southern and the northern kingdom, brought back together through Christ. The middle wall of partition was the animal sacrifice that was against us: when Christ came on the scene he abolished animal sacrifice, and it was never prophesied that Israel would be joined back together through animal sacrifice, only through Jesus the Christ.

So these Christians in America do not know what they are talking about. It is a racist lie. Christianity is nothing but white supremacy, because it is not backed up with the Bible whatsoever.

precepts.why: To understand the our and the us, go to the top of the letter: “Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, to the saints which are at Ephesus.” The letter is written to the saints. So the question is, who are the saints according to the holy scriptures?

“He also exalteth the horn of his people, the praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel, a people near unto him. Praise ye the Lord.” The saints are the children of Israel.

When the captains dealt with Fred Price and brought out this scripture, he asked, are you saying all the saints in the New Testament have to be the children of Israel? Yes. Christianity has never been able to show another definition of saints in the scripture, and it cannot. The only saints in the scriptures are the 12 tribes of Israel. So the us of Ephesians 2 is the nation of Israel, and the Ephesians are not blacks and whites coming together.

They will say, you have to deal with those strangers in Ephesians 2:12. So see what the strangers are. “The God of this people of Israel chose our fathers, and exalted the people when they dwelt as strangers in the land of Egypt.” The book of Acts says the God of Israel chose our fathers; those speaking in Antioch were Israelites. And the people that dwelt as strangers in Egypt were Israel. So the strangers are the nation of Israel, the Israelites.

“Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia.” The strangers again, and they are scattered.

Put the map up: Asia is Asia Minor, and there you see Ephesus, and next to it Colosse. That is what this class is dealing with. Pastor Pam mentioned Ephesus, which is right there in Asia next to Colosse, and the strangers scattered in Asia are Israelites.

Ephesians 2:12 speaks of the covenants of promise. Paul tells who they belong to: “Who are Israelites; to whom pertaineth the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the giving of the law, and the service of God, and the promises; Whose are the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came.”

The covenants and the promises pertain to the Israelites, and Christ came for the Israelites. No other nation. Not Pam and all those other Christians out there.

Who was far off? “But fear not thou, O my servant Jacob, and be not dismayed, O Israel: for, behold, I will save thee from afar off.” It is Israel who is afar off. It is really that simple: the ones in Ephesians 2:13 who sometimes were far off and are made nigh by the blood of Christ are Israel.

It says he is our peace, so go to the Prince of Peace. “For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given”: unto us, that is possessive. “And the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.”

“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end, upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom.” When it is time for Christ to return and the Israelites to reign, there will not be any end.

Then it says who it is for: “The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it hath lighted upon Israel.” So our peace is Israel’s peace. Christ is the peace that brings both nations, the southern and the northern kingdom, back together. That is the both made one of Ephesians 2:14.

This is the prophecy of the both made one. “Behold, I will take the children of Israel from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land.” He gathers the children of Israel from among the heathen, so there would be Israelites living in places like Galatia, Ephesus and Colosse.

“And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all.” That is exactly what Ephesians 2:14 says: he made them one. He is our peace, the Israelites’ peace. It was never black and white.

sense.text:
Christians fail to understand that Acts is the basis of the New Testament. Paul’s epistles, first and second Peter, James: Acts gives the understanding of them. If you get confused on a verse, go back to Acts 2:5 and it will tell you who the audience is.

“And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.” Jews out of every nation: the children of Israel scattered among the heathen, like we just read in Ezekiel 37.

precepts.why: Of the devout Jews out of every nation, the list includes “Parthians, and Medes, and Elamites, and the dwellers in Mesopotamia, and in Judea, and Cappadocia, in Pontus, and Asia.” Asia, Asia Minor, where Ephesus and Colosse are, right next to each other. Israelites were dwelling in Asia, and that is where this class is going.

sense.text: “Paul having passed through the upper coasts came to Ephesus.” The Apostle Paul came unto Ephesus. That is why the map keeps going up: look how close Ephesus is to Colosse, Ephesus to the left and Colosse to the right.

precepts.why:
“And this continued by the space of two years; so that all they which dwelt in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus.” All they which dwelt in Asia, so Colosse heard the word that Paul was preaching.

In the book of Acts you will not find Paul going to Colosse. But it is there, because Colosse is next to Ephesus, which is in Asia. So if you ever wondered why you can’t find the precept for Colosse in Acts, that is your precept right there.

sense.text:
Ephesus was a great city: the big theater, and Diana of the Ephesians.

“To the saints and faithful brethren in Christ which are at Colosse.” Just like Ephesians is written to the saints at Ephesus, this is the same concept: the saints in Colosse. These are Israelites in Asia.

“Since we heard of your faith in Christ Jesus, and of the love which ye have to all the saints.” Paul is saying he never went to Colosse. The spirit was so heavy in Ephesus that it spread all throughout Asia, and Paul ended up hearing there was another church over in Colosse, fervent in spirit too, so he wrote to them.

On the map you have Ephesus in the middle, Colosse to the right of it, and above it Laodicea, which you read about in Revelation, and Hierapolis. Colosse was known as one of the wealthy cities of that region, and the gospel spread through all those cities.

“Which is come unto you, as it is in all the world; and bringeth forth fruit, as it doth also in you, since the day ye heard of it, and knew the grace of God in truth.” This is the spread of the gospel throughout Asia, and specifically to Colosse. The word came unto them as it came in all the world, and brought forth fruit in them too.

“As ye also learned of Epaphras our dear fellowservant, who is for you a faithful minister of Christ.” How did the church at Colosse hear and learn? Through Epaphras. That is how they woke up: this brother heard it and said, I’m going to teach all of you.

That is just like today, when somebody sees IUIC on YouTube and says, I have to print out these flyers and start hitting the city, and then this school pops up, then that school pops up. We are the continuation of the acts of the apostles. When we read these scriptures we have to put ourselves in them and envision how the forefathers were, because we are doing the exact same thing.

Epaphras was a self-starter. He did not need someone right there to get the ground running. He said, that’s true, I believe it, I’m going to go teach that. A faithful minister of Christ.
“Who also declared unto us your love in the Spirit.” Epaphras brought word back to Paul of the Colossians.

precepts.why: Paul said he heard of their faith, though he did not visit them. “For I would that ye knew what great conflict I have for you, and for them at Laodicea, and for as many as have not seen my face in the flesh.” Why had they not seen Paul’s face? Because he never went to Laodicea and he never went to Colosse. The word reached them through others.

The gospel came unto them as in all the world. In Ephesus they said, “not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul hath persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they be no gods, which are made with hands.” Turned away from idolatry, to serving the one true God and believing on Jesus the Christ.

“The temple of the great goddess Diana should be despised, and her magnificence should be destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worshippeth.” Colosse, just like Ephesus and the rest of the world, was worshipping Diana. They worshipped the woman, just like America worships the Virgin Mary: women deities, women’s rights, liberation, all of that. It is the same thing.

But the spirit was so heavy on the Apostle Paul that places he did not physically go were getting touched. It is marvelous. It is like Joppa and Caesarea in Acts 9 and 10, close to each other: it was just spreading throughout Asia.

An example of the same concept. “After these things Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth”: the church at Corinth. Then: “And Crispus, the chief ruler of the synagogue, believed on the Lord with all his house; and many of the Corinthians hearing believed, and were baptized.”

If you were in the synagogue you were practicing the law of sacrifice, just like a lot of us were practicing Christianity. But he believed on Christ, and it started with him, and the others took hold of it. Paul was actually there in Corinth, though. With Epaphras it was different: he took the word and ran with it himself.

More on Epaphras. “Epaphras, who is one of you, a servant of Christ, saluteth you, always labouring fervently for you in prayers, that ye may stand perfect and complete in all the will of God.” He is one of them, a Colossian.

“For I bear him record, that he hath a great zeal for you, and them that are in Laodicea, and them in Hierapolis.” On the map, Colosse, Laodicea and Hierapolis are all in that same region. Epaphras was putting in mad work.

“There salute thee Epaphras, my fellowprisoner in Christ Jesus.” Paul calls Epaphras his fellow prisoner. Why is he mentioned in the epistle to Philemon? Because Philemon was also from Colosse.

“Marcus, Aristarchus, Demas, Lucas, my fellowlabourers.” Remember Demas: when you read Timothy, Demas went off and forsook this truth.

“Paul, a prisoner of Jesus Christ, and Timothy our brother, unto Philemon our dearly beloved, and fellowlabourer, And to our beloved Apphia, and Archippus our fellowsoldier, and to the church in thy house.” It started with Epaphras, and then others came: Philemon, and a church in his house. That is how the work spread in that region.

sense.text: “The salutation by the hand of me Paul. Remember my bonds. Grace be with you. Amen. Written from Rome to the Colossians by Tychicus and Onesimus.” Not every Bible has that last line, so it is put on the screen for everyone. The epistle was written from Rome, where Paul was in bonds, to the church at Colosse, and carried by Tychicus and Onesimus.
“All my state shall Tychicus declare unto you, who is a beloved brother, and a faithful minister and fellowservant in the Lord.” Tychicus is one of the two who carried the letter to Colosse.

“With Onesimus, a faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you. They shall make known unto you all things which are done here.” Onesimus, the other one who carried the letter, is one of them, a Colossian.

“Aristarchus my fellowprisoner saluteth you, and Marcus, sister’s son to Barnabas.” If Marcus is Barnabas’ sister’s son, that makes Marcus his nephew. That is John Mark, and he is the one Paul and Barnabas had their dispute over at the end of Acts 15.

precepts.why:
“And Barnabas determined to take with them John, whose surname was Mark. But Paul thought not good to take him with them, who departed from them from Pamphylia, and went not with them to the work.” Not just anybody could travel. Paul gave him a chance, and when it came to the work he was nowhere to be found; he came up missing.

“And the contention was so sharp between them, that they departed asunder one from the other: and so Barnabas took Mark, and sailed unto Cyprus; And Paul chose Silas, and departed.” Paul said straight, I don’t care if that is your nephew, I’m not taking him to travel with me no more. Barnabas was sticking up for John Mark because he was his sister’s son. Colossians 4:10 lets you understand that dynamic.

“I beseech thee for my son Onesimus, whom I have begotten in my bonds.” Why would Paul beseech Philemon on behalf of Onesimus? Because they had to be in the same place, Colosse. Onesimus is one of you, and so is Philemon. That proves who the Colossians are: these are Israelites.

Ephesians, Colossians, Philemon, Philippians, 1 Timothy, Titus and 2 Timothy were all written in the same period. “And Tychicus have I sent to Ephesus.” Ephesus is right there next to Colosse. The same Tychicus Paul sent to Ephesus he sent unto the Colossians: “whom I have sent unto you for the same purpose, that he might know your estate, and comfort your hearts; With Onesimus, a faithful and beloved brother, who is one of you.” Onesimus is one of them, whom we read about in Philemon.

sense.text: “Even the mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations, but now is made manifest to his saints.” Once again it uses the term saints: Israel. The Colossians are Israelites.

“To whom God would make known what is the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles.” The mystery is that the northern kingdom, who are the Gentiles, can come back into the fold.

“Which is Christ in you, the hope of glory.” You had no hope unless Christ came and died for us. There was no repentance and no reconciliation except through Christ.

precepts.why: There is a Christian out there watching, so prove who the Gentiles are: “The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles.” Zebulun and Naphtali are Israelite tribes of the northern kingdom, and they are called the Gentiles. So the mystery among the Gentiles in Colossians 1:27 is the northern kingdom coming back in.

A chart of the time, about 60 to 67 AD, when Paul was under house arrest in Rome, as in Acts 28, shows Ephesians, Colossians, Philemon, Philippians, 1 Timothy, Titus and 2 Timothy written in that time. The books overlap and speak of the same topics because Paul wrote them at the same time and to that region.

So Ephesians speaks of the same mystery: “How that by revelation he made known unto me the mystery.” And: “Which in other ages was not made known unto the sons of men, as it is now revealed unto his holy apostles and prophets by the Spirit; That the Gentiles should be fellowheirs.”

That is the mystery: the animal sacrifice is done away with and no longer in play, and the northern and southern kingdom now have a chance to come back into the fold with Christ. “And of the same body, and partakers of his promise in Christ by the gospel.” Partakers of his promise, the covenant. The promises were not made through animal sacrifice; the promises were made through Christ.

sense.text: “If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above, where Christ sitteth on the right hand of God.” If you be risen with Christ means if you decide to repent and now follow Christ: then this is what you do. If you don’t want to accept Christ, it is not for you. All Israel is not Israel, just as Romans 9:6 says.

precepts.why: Those who are risen with Christ come through the Christ seed. “Now to Abraham and his seed were the promises made.” Unto Abraham and his seed, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, from which came the 12 tribes of Israel. “He saith not, And to seeds, as of many”: he does not say to every nation, only that chosen lineage. “But as of one, And to thy seed, which is Christ.” Through that lineage came Jesus the Christ.

Then jump down: “Wherefore then serveth the law? It was added because of transgressions, till the seed should come to whom the promise was made”. The seed, which is Christ, should come to whom the promise was made. Who was the promise made to? The 12 tribes of Israel. So as soon as Christ came on the scene, animal sacrifice was done away with.

“And it was ordained by angels in the hand of a mediator. Now a mediator is not a mediator of one, but God is one.”

“Is he the God of the Jews only?” Is he only for the southern kingdom? “Is he not also of the Gentiles? Yes, of the Gentiles also”: the northern kingdom also. “Seeing it is one God, which shall justify the circumcision by faith, and uncircumcision through faith.” One God justifies both houses through faith.

“Is the law then against the promises of God? God forbid: for if there had been a law given which could have given life, verily righteousness should have been by the law. But the scripture hath concluded all under sin, that the promise by faith of Jesus Christ might be given to them that believe.”

The promise is the topic of discussion, and it is given to them that believe. It is not talking about everybody. From verse 16 it lets you know it is the Israelites that believe on Christ who get the promises. So there should be no confusion about who is risen with Christ in Colossians 3:1.

sense.text:
“Where there is neither Greek nor Jew, circumcision nor uncircumcision, Barbarian, Scythian, bond nor free: but Christ is all, and in all.” A Christian would throw away all the proof, all those facts, because of this one verse and say, Greeks, Barbarians, Scythians, those are the other nations. Really? After reading all of that in context? No.

Greek: the Encyclopedia of the Jewish Diaspora says it is common knowledge that the Jews of the western diaspora knew only Greek. They knew neither Hebrew nor Aramaic, and their prayer and the reading of the Torah were in Greek. The sages recognized there were whole diaspora communities that spoke only Greek, and the places named in Acts 2, in the journeys of Paul and in the Pauline epistles give the picture of the western Jewish Greek-speaking diaspora. So some of our people were called Greeks and some were called Jews, because of a language difference, but we are still the same people.

Circumcision is the Jews, the southern kingdom; uncircumcision is the northern kingdom, the Gentiles.

Barbarian is from the Greek barbaros, used among the early Greeks to describe all foreigners, including the Romans. If you were not a Greek, they called you a barbarian, and we were scattered throughout the four corners of the earth.

Scythian: in Israel Redivivus, Frederick Charles Danvers writes that the tribes of Israel were divided into families and subtribes, and at a later date many tribes bearing different names were collectively known to the Greeks as Scythians, the nomadic people of that area. So we are the Barbarians. We are the Scythians. We are the Greeks. Get mad, we don’t care: this is our book and not yours.

“But Christ is all, and in all.” Now they will say Christ is in all. No: Lord of all Israel.

precepts.why:
We were the Romans too, and mainstream Christianity does not understand that today. Of the devout Jews, the list goes on: “Phrygia, and Pamphylia, in Egypt, and in the parts of Libya about Cyrene, and strangers of Rome.”

Then back to verse 5: “And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.” Jews out of every nation. We were called Romans. We were called Greeks. We were called Barbarians.

“James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.” We were scattered throughout the four corners of the earth, so why would it be a surprise that we were called Greeks and Barbarians? Esau, with a demonic self, is trying to insert himself, and that is how they were able to deceive the masses.

When they say Christ is all and in all means every nation: “Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him.” In every nation, because Israel was scattered into every nation.

Then read who it was sent to: “The word which God sent unto the children of Israel, preaching peace by Jesus Christ: (he is Lord of all:)”. Lord of all: Lord of all Israel. That is the all of Colossians 3:11.

sense.text:
“Put on therefore, as the elect of God, holy and beloved.” After he refers to us as the Greeks, the Barbarians, the Scythians, in verse 12 he calls us the elect of God. He speaks in a language we can understand, not for the heathen to understand. Just in case you were confused by what Paul was saying in verse 11, he clears it up in verse 12. Holy means severed, separated from all other nations on the face of the earth.

They know good and well this Bible does not belong to them. But in slavery they played on our ignorance. We could not read or write, everything they taught us was oral tradition, they would not let us read the Bible, and in the slave Bible they gave us the majority of the Bible was not even there. They wanted to keep us docile, ignorant and misinformed. But there is a God, the God of Israel, who has poured his spirit upon his people in these last days, and now we know what the Bible is talking about.

“Bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering.”

“Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another, if any man have a quarrel against any: even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye.” The Lord, through the Apostle Paul, is instructing the Colossians how to deal with one another, because we are the same people. We are the sons and daughters of the living God, and there is a way we have to govern ourselves and treat each other.

precepts.why: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect.” The elect of God in Colossians 3:12 is Israel.

Leviticus tells us how to be holy, and it is only for Israel. “And ye shall be holy unto me: for I the Lord am holy, and have severed you from other people, that ye should be mine.” He has severed us. So in Colossians 3:12 it is not all nations: holy means severed, separated from all other nations, that ye Israelites should be his people.
Beloved: “He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.” The holy and beloved of Colossians 3:12 is Israel.

sense.text:
“Servants, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh; not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but in singleness of heart, fearing God.” This is one they have used throughout history. Now that we have the understanding, precept upon precept and in context, these servants have to be Israelites, and the masters have to be Israelites. They cherry-picked this scripture to fit their evil narrative, and the Lord sees it all and has not forgotten what they have done.

The Religious Instruction of the Negroes in the United States shows how they did it. It counts the slaves and free persons of color in the census of 1790 and calls the original stock a people in a state of absolute heathenism. They inserted themselves as the people and made us the heathen.

In 1673 Baxter published his Christian Directory with directions for masters in foreign plantations who have negroes and other slaves. In their evil minds they really believed they were the masters. Did the Lord allow it to happen? Absolutely. But that is not what Colossians 3:22 is talking about. They told the masters to remember the slaves are equally capable of salvation with yourselves; that is where that false sense of equality comes from: slavery and Christianity. They said God is their absolute owner, and that is correct, God is our owner; but that they and you are equally under the government and laws of God is incorrect. We are not equal with these people. They said God is their reconciled tender father, and you cannot reconcile what was never close to God; if reconciliation is for the slaves, they know who we are.

They called themselves Christ’s trustees, the guardians of our souls, and said they must exercise both power and love to bring us to the knowledge and faith of Christ, opening the Bible and saying what they wanted it to say. They told masters to teach us the way to heaven and to carry themselves as redeemed with us, to live with us in glory. They want us to go to heaven and live with them. No, that is called hell. That mind control from slavery is why a brother on the street says, if he goes to hell, I’m going too: he does not want to go anywhere without his master.

In the eye of the law we were property. By law or custom we were excluded from education, and by consequence from the reading of the word of God, thrown for religious instruction upon oral communications entirely. If we were equal, why were we excluded from education? Because they did not want us to know that servants obey your masters is not talking about them. So if we wanted to learn about God, we had to go through the white man, and to this day, if it does not come out of the white man’s mouth, our people don’t fully believe it. We go precept upon precept and they still can’t see it.

The Willie Lynch letter says the slave, after receiving this indoctrination, shall carry on and become self-refuelling and self-generating for hundreds of years, maybe thousands; that distrust is stronger than trust and envy stronger than adulation; set old against young and dark-skinned against light-skinned; have the white servants and overseers distrust all blacks, but make the slaves trust and depend on us, love, respect and trust only us. That is us today: distrust among our own, and anything the white man says is gold.

They would not let us have church organizations independent of their own, so that we would depend on them more strongly; they said they could forbid religious meetings, forbid servants going to church at all, or send them only to churches they selected, and literally shut up the kingdom of heaven against men. They believe they are God. They wrote that the Negroes were in a state of almost absolute dependence upon their owners for the words of eternal life, and the most needy of any people in the country. At any time these things can happen again, as we read in the time of the Maccabees: Trump is trying to make America great again because everybody sees the rise of the Israelites, they push Christian nationalism, and JD Vance said anybody speaking against America, reject them.

That is how bad we have been destroyed: Brandon Tatum says black people were better off during slavery and agrees with Charlie Kirk; a white pastor says God blessed black Americans through white people and slavery, and Tatum agrees; Tatum cried when Charlie Kirk died but mocks our own people standing up when one of our brothers died mysteriously in a racist town in Mississippi known for lynching. Yes, we are activists: we stand up for righteousness and speak against the evils done to our people, and that puts fear in our oppressors.

After all of that, back to the verse in context: obey your masters in singleness of heart, fearing God. These masters were taking care of the servants’ clothes, raiment, housing and food. Why would you disrespect them? Number one, that is your brother; and number two, he is doing this for you. As you do your duties, you work and they take care of you.

precepts.why: The Lord said they would call us heathen. “Thus saith the Lord God; Because that Moab and Seir do say, Behold, the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen.” How did we become like the heathen? By following after the heathen: celebrating their pagan rituals, Christmas and Thanksgiving, eating crab, shrimp, pork and lobster, praying to a white man. That is what made us heathenistic.

Our enemies would like to think God cast us away and will not redeem us. Even with us becoming heathens, this is what the Lord says: “Know ye therefore that they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham. And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, saying, In thee shall all nations be blessed.”

Foreseeing: the Lord already knew we were going to become heathens. He saw that this would happen to us. They can get mad all over again; it does not matter, we are still God’s chosen people. And that justification through faith in Christ is only for one people.
“In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.” The justification is for the seed of Israel. Yes, we became heathen, but we are still going to be justified through Christ.

They believe they can be saved, and us with them, they being the people. Who is salvation for? “Him hath God exalted with his right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel, and forgiveness of sins.” A saviour brings salvation, and that salvation is only for the children of Israel.

Their book calls God our reconciled father. But reconciliation is not for everybody. Re means to do again: repeat, redo. Reconciliation cannot apply to the other nations, because they were never a people close or near to God; the Israelites are the only ones that have been near to God.

“Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.” That is referring to Christ: through Christ we get our reconciliation, and it is upon thy people, Israel.

They told the masters to serve their necessities by their slaves so as to prefer God’s interest, and to teach them the way to heaven. “Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things.” In want of all things: we wanted food, clothing, housing and shelter, and we got that old-time religion from them too.

Read again after hearing one of our own say we were better off during slavery: “and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” The yoke of iron is off our neck, which means we have been destroyed as a people, to the point that in the present day our own people say we were better off in slavery. If he says that, you already know how he looks at his own people: in hate and disgust.

In the eye of their law we were their property. “Wherefore doeth the Lord our God all these things unto us? then shalt thou answer them, Like as ye have forsaken me, and served strange gods in your land, so shall ye serve strangers in a land that is not yours.” We are serving strangers in a land that is not ours.
“Servants have ruled over us: there is none that doth deliver us out of their hand.” This is Bible prophecy.

It happened in the time of Assyria, Babylon, Persia, Greece, Rome, and America in the present day. It keeps happening over and over again because we are the people of God. “I will liken my judgment unto a ring”: a circular motion. The curse comes right back around. But this is the last time.

We were their property and they still view us as that. They may have said equal in salvation, but while we were here they treated us like beasts in chattel slavery; we were known as three-fifths of a man. They never looked at us as their equals.

“And it yieldeth much increase unto the kings whom thou hast set over us because of our sins”: this is happening because we sinned against our God. “Also they have dominion over our bodies, and over our cattle, at their pleasure, and we are in great distress.” Dominion over our bodies, to look at us as their property.

They could forbid religious meetings. This went on during the Inquisition as well, when Christianity was changed into the all-inclusive Catholic church: they went around killing the real Jews, tearing up our safe houses and taking our book. The same thing is going to happen again, because now we know the truth, and the only way the lie can hold is to destroy everyone who does not go along with it.

He deceives them that dwell on the earth, “saying to them that dwell on the earth, that they should make an image to the beast, which had the wound by a sword, and did live.” That is the false image of Christ. “And cause that as many as would not worship the image of the beast should be killed.” If we did not agree, we were killed. Our people knew it was not true, but they did not want to be killed, so they went with the lie, generation after generation. But there is a new generation on the earth, and we are not accepting the lies anymore. We know we are the people, and we know what comes with the territory.

Their book says the Negroes are the most needy of any people in the country. We are the needy, and that is in the Bible referring to us. “The instruments also of the churl are evil: he deviseth wicked devices to destroy the poor with lying words, even when the needy speaketh right.” Even when we are speaking out of the Bible, they devour us and call it hate speech.

Tatum thinks white people just switched and started loving us after they let us out of slavery. “Thou didst strike through with his staves the head of his villages: they came out as a whirlwind to scatter me.” When Christ returns, the same people who had us in slavery are going to try to fight against Christ.

“Their rejoicing was as to devour the poor secretly.” Secretly: even after the Emancipation Proclamation in 1863 it was not over. Then came the school-to-prison pipeline, redlining, sundown towns, sharecropping. It is still the same thing. He is still setting traps and still oppressing us to this day.
Who are the poor they devour secretly? “That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.” The poor of his people: Israel.

Tatum asks if we have nothing better to do. What is better than standing up for God and standing up for his people, getting your household in order, not committing fornication and adultery, taking care of your household? “And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men.” We always have to do what is right for God and for our people.

When these things happen to our people, we are going to be there and we are not going to stop, coons among our own people or not. “Therefore thou deliveredst them into the hand of their enemies, who vexed them”: that is what happened to us. “And in the time of their trouble, when they cried unto thee, thou heardest them from heaven”: the Lord is starting to hear our cry. We are supposed to pray unto the Lord until he brings vengeance.

“And according to thy manifold mercies thou gavest them saviours, who saved them out of the hand of their enemies.” That is happening through the purple and gold going to this city and that country, teaching the word of God. Those are the saviours, and the saviours showed up in Ocean Springs, Mississippi.

A white man in Cicero, Illinois in 1966 said, the ones that are going to march, I don’t like. They don’t like it because when we march we have our pride, our dignity, respect and confidence. They don’t like when we stand up as the nation of Israel; it angers them and makes them afraid.

We have been marching; Marcus Garvey was marching back in the day. “But Pharaoh shall not hearken unto you, that I may lay my hand upon Egypt, and bring forth mine armies, and my people the children of Israel, out of the land of Egypt by great judgments.” We have been marching. We marched around the walls of Jericho.

They do not like when we stand up on our feet with confidence as the nation of Israel, not as blacks. “And after three days and an half the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them.” Great fear falls on them when they see us rise up as the children of God, the army of the living God.

Tatum says black Hebrew Israelites are nowhere to be found in the community. That is a lie: we teach in the hoods and the ghettos where our people are every day. O Block in Chicago, East St. Louis, Memphis, Miami, Compton, LA, Philly.

“And they taught in Judah, and had the book of the law of the Lord with them, and went about throughout all the cities of Judah, and taught the people.” We go to our people just like the forefathers did, and we bring the Bible with us. We don’t just go to one city or one state; wherever our people are scattered and afflicted, we are there.

Pastor Pam says the gospel can’t be for one ethnicity only, and that this is a heretical doctrine of cultic ministries. It’s you, Pam: “I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.” It is only for one nation, 12 tribes. If you are not part of that, you are not getting in.

“And had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel.” The kingdom is only for God’s people. Some of our people are bugged out, and it is a direct correlation to slavery.

“If a servant say to his master, I will not do as it pleaseth thee; though afterward he do it, he angereth him that nourisheth him.” The servant who refuses is not just angering the master; he is also angering the Lord that nourisheth us.

sense.text:
“Masters, give unto your servants that which is just and equal.” They said they were the masters. Did they do that? No. They lived in the big house and we lived in the outhouse, and when we got emancipated they never gave us the 40 acres and a mule. They are showing that they are hypocrites and impostors, the damn devil that the Bible speaks of.

“Knowing that ye also have a Master in heaven.” Colossians, Ephesians and Philemon were all written at about the same time, and they say the same thing about servants and masters.

precepts.why: “Servants, be obedient to them that are your masters according to the flesh, with fear and trembling, in singleness of your heart, as unto Christ; Not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but as the servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart.” The same teaching as Colossians, written in the same time to the same region: doing the will of God from the heart.

More on these servants: “That every man should let his manservant, and every man his maidservant, being an Hebrew or an Hebrewess, go free; that none should serve himself of them, to wit, of a Jew his brother.” These servants are Israelites, a Jew his brother.

“Let as many servants as are under the yoke count their own masters worthy of all honour, that the name of God and his doctrine be not blasphemed.” Under the yoke of bondage. If you have a master who still believes in the law of sacrifice, but you believe in Christ, you still honor him and treat him with respect.

“And they that have believing masters, let them not despise them, because they are brethren.” Israelite masters who believe on Christ: don’t despise your brother. Not one time has the Lord ever said we are brothers with the other nations. So those masters are Israelites.

Now this makes more sense. “There is neither Jew nor Greek”: we went over that in Colossians 3:11 with the Greek-speaking Jews. “There is neither bond nor free”: the Israelite servant or the Israelite master. “There is neither male nor female”: the manservant and the maidservant, the Israelite man and the Israelite woman. “For ye are all one in Christ Jesus.” We are all one nation under Christ. That is all it is talking about.
“For unto me the children of Israel are servants; they are my servants whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: I am the Lord your God.” Israel are the Lord’s servants.

When we read the context precept upon precept, we see we have been lied to as a people. “Who art thou that judgest another man’s servant? to his own master he standeth or falleth.” Our real master is Christ. “Yea, he shall be holden up: for God is able to make him stand.”

They changed the narrative and flipped the script, inserting themselves where they are not. But they are in the scriptures, and this is how they are there: “Both thy bondmen, and thy bondmaids, which thou shalt have, shall be of the heathen that are round about you; of them shall ye buy bondmen and bondmaids.”

Since they wanted to go outside their natural design as our bondmen and bondmaids, slaves, the Lord says they are going back to that. “Moreover of the children of the strangers that do sojourn among you, of them shall ye buy, and of their families that are with you, which they begat in your land: and they shall be your possession.” They were originally our possession; we sinned against our God and became their possession. But it is going back to the way it is supposed to be.

“And ye shall take them as an inheritance for your children after you, to inherit them for a possession; they shall be your bondmen for ever.” For how long? Forever.

“Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession.” The Lord is going to give us the heathen for our inheritance. We are going to own them.

“Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron; thou shalt dash them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.” If they don’t want to get right, boom, upside the head. “Be wise now therefore, O ye kings: be instructed, ye judges of the earth.”

Esau thinks he can change his judgment. No: God said it, it is in writing, it is stamped, and he is going back into slavery. “I know that, whatsoever God doeth, it shall be for ever: nothing can be put to it, nor any thing taken from it: and God doeth it, that men should fear before him.” Nothing can be put to it to change it.

“For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land: and the strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob. And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place.” The people, God’s chosen people, are going to take the strangers and put them in their own place. You thought you were coming in the kingdom? No, you can’t come up in here with us: back to Mount Seir, back to your caves, dwelling in the mountains.

“And the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids.” Because that is why they were created in the first place; that is their role, forever. “And they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.”

sense.text: “And when this epistle is read among you, cause that it be read also in the church of the Laodiceans; and that ye likewise read the epistle from Laodicea.” Laodicea was right there next to Colosse. It may not be mentioned in the book of Acts, but put the map up with the churches of Asia, Philadelphia, Sardis, all of them right there by Colosse, and it connects: you get a better understanding of Asia.

precepts.why: “What thou seest, write in a book, and send it unto the seven churches which are in Asia.” The seven churches in Asia are Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamos, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia and Laodicea, and Laodicea was right there next to Colosse.

sense.text: “All this have I seen, and applied my heart unto every work that is done under the sun: there is a time wherein one man ruleth over another to his own hurt.” That is Esau. The way Esau treated us is going to be to his own detriment.

precepts.why: Yes, we sinned against our God, and yes, the Lord allowed us to go into the hands of our enemies, but they took it too far. “And I am very sore displeased with the heathen that are at ease: for I was but a little displeased, and they helped forward the affliction.” They helped forward the affliction, and Christ saw it.

“In all their affliction he was afflicted.” Through all our slavery, the Lord saw all of it. When he comes back he is going to feel all of that pain and suffering they did to the children of Israel, and he is going to wreak havoc on these nations. “And the angel of his presence saved them.” Salvation is not for the oppressors; salvation is for those who have been afflicted.

sense.text: “The proud have digged pits for me, which are not after thy law.” The proud dig pits for God’s people. They are not after God’s laws: how come you can abort in America? How come gay marriage is legalized? They don’t keep or uphold God’s laws, but a lot of coons out there follow behind the white man. They are not after God’s commandments.

precepts.why: Who is the proud? “The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?”

“The vision of Obadiah. Thus saith the Lord God concerning Edom.” Edom is Esau: your friendly neighborhood white man, the Europeans and the Americans. They are the proud who have digged pits for God’s people.

sense.text: “Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein.” They thought evil against us, but the Lord meant it for good. Jacob is going to win in the end. “And he that setteth a trap shall be taken therein.”
“He that worketh mischief, it shall fall upon him, and he shall not know whence it cometh.” He will not know, because his pride has deceived him.
“Mockery and reproach are from the proud.” That is all they do: they falsely accuse us and mock us. “But vengeance, as a lion, shall lie in wait for them.”

“They that rejoice at the fall of the righteous shall be taken in the snare.” Remember when they said, raze it, raze it, to the ground. The Lord has not forgotten. “And anguish shall consume them before they die.” It does not pay to be wicked, and it does not pay to follow after your oppressor, because in the end they are going to be destroyed.

precepts.why: That is what they do: they work mischief and then call it law. “Shall the throne of iniquity have fellowship with thee, which frameth mischief by a law?” Two men getting married, two women getting married, all these laws; everything done since Trump came into office, the firing and the DEI hires, all of it against us. They frame mischief and call it law.

Vengeance as a lion: “The lion is come up from his thicket, and the destroyer of the Gentiles is on his way; he is gone forth from his place to make thy land desolate; and thy cities shall be laid waste, without an inhabitant.” That is twofold: it is talking about Nebuchadnezzar, and it is talking about Christ.

sense.text: “Let favour be shewed to the wicked, yet will he not learn righteousness.” If favor were shown to Esau, he still would not change his wicked ways. “In the land of uprightness will he deal unjustly”: the land of uprightness is the land of Israel, and he stole it. “And will not behold the majesty of the Lord”: he changed his image to a white man with stringy blond hair and blue eyes.

“Lord, when thy hand is lifted up, they will not see: but they shall see, and be ashamed for their envy at the people.” The people is God’s chosen people. “Yea, the fire of thine enemies shall devour them.”
“Lord, thou wilt ordain peace for us.” Remember Ephesians 2: he is going to ordain peace for us and destruction for our enemies. “For thou also hast wrought all our works in us.”
“O Lord our God, other lords beside thee have had dominion over us.” Like the so-called white man, like the Babylonians, like the Assyrians. “But by thee only will we make mention of thy name.”

“They are dead, they shall not live; they are deceased, they shall not rise: therefore hast thou visited and destroyed them, and made all their memory to perish.” All our enemies, all the other lords that had rule over us, are dead.

precepts.why: Who are the people they envy? “The heathen shall envy thee, but they shall be able to do nothing against thee, saith the Lord.” The heathen shall envy the Israelites, and they can’t stop it, because they are not going to be in rulership or ownership anymore.
